subject: Chemistry
question: In the unbranched Alkane homologous series at room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$), the first four members ($\text{CH}_4$ to $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$) exist physically as:

options.A: Colorless, odorless gases

explanation: Methane, ethane, propane, and butane ($C_1$ to $C_4$) have low molar masses and weak London dispersion forces, keeping them in the gaseous state at $25^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Chemistry
question: Complete combustion of Methane ($\text{CH}_4$) in an excess supply of oxygen yields which products?

options.A: Carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$), Water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), and Heat

explanation: $\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Heat} (890\text{ kJ/mol})$. Complete combustion of hydrocarbons produces carbon dioxide and water vapor.

subject: Chemistry
question: In the photochemical chlorination of Methane in diffused sunlight, what reactive intermediates drive the chain propagation steps?

options.A: Chlorine free radicals ($\text{Cl}^\bullet$) and Methyl radicals ($\text{CH}_3^\bullet$)

explanation: Photochemical halogenation follows a free radical mechanism: $\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{Cl}^ullet$, followed by $\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{HCl}$.

subject: Chemistry
question: What is the general molecular formula for aliphatic mono-unsaturated Alkenes (Olefins)?

options.A: $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$

explanation: Alkenes contain one carbon-carbon double bond ($\text{C}=\text{C}$) and have the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$ (e.g. Ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$).

subject: Chemistry
question: When reddish-brown Bromine water ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is shaken with an unsaturated hydrocarbon (such as Ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$), the observation is:

options.A: The reddish-brown color is immediately discharged (decolorized) due to addition across the double bond
options.B: A dense purple precipitate is formed
options.C: The solution turns bright yellow with no decolorization
options.D: Vigorous evolution of hydrogen gas occurs

explanation: Ethene undergoes rapid electrophilic addition with $\text{Br}_2$ to yield colorless 1,2-dibromoethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$), decolorizing the bromine water.

subject: Chemistry
question: Baeyer's reagent is used as a qualitative test to identify double or triple bonds. It consists of:

options.A: Cold, dilute, alkaline Potassium Permanganate solution ($\text{KMnO}_4$)
options.D: Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid and Zinc amalgam

explanation: Baeyer's reagent is $1\%$ alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$; unsaturated hydrocarbons decolorize the purple solution and form brown $\text{MnO}_2$ precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
question: In the laboratory, Ethyne (Acetylene gas, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) is conveniently generated at room temperature by the reaction of water with:

options.A: Calcium Carbide ($\text{CaC}_2$)

explanation: $\text{CaC}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_2\uparrow + \text{Ca(OH)}_2$. Hydrolysis of solid calcium carbide generates ethyne gas rapidly at ambient conditions.

subject: Chemistry
question: The industrial conversion of liquid vegetable oils into solid vegetable ghee (margarine) is an addition reaction known as catalytic hydrogenation, conducted using:

options.A: Hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$) in the presence of Nickel ($\text{Ni}$) catalyst at $200^\circ\text{C}$

explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation adds hydrogen across carbon-carbon double bonds in unsaturated fatty acid chains in the presence of a finely divided Ni catalyst.

subject: Chemistry
question: Ethyne (Acetylene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) burned in pure oxygen produces an extremely hot flame ($~3000^\circ\text{C}$) widely used in industry for:

options.A: Oxy-acetylene welding and cutting of metals

explanation: The oxy-acetylene flame reaches over $3000^\circ\text{C}$, providing intense concentrated heat for melting, welding, and cutting structural steel.

subject: Chemistry
question: Under high temperature and pressure in the presence of a catalyst, thousands of Ethene molecules link together by addition polymerization to produce:

options.A: Polyethylene (Polythene plastic)

explanation: $n(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2) \rightarrow -(\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2)_n-$. Ethene monomers polymerize to form polythene, the world's most widely manufactured thermoplastic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Free Radical Halogenation Mechanism of Methane
question: In the photochemical chlorination of Methane ($\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$), the homolytic cleavage of the $\text{Cl}-\text{Cl}$ bond by UV light represents which step?

options.A: Chain Initiation Step

explanation: Chain initiation involves homolytic fission of the chlorine molecule under UV radiation: $\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{Cl}^\bullet$, generating reactive free radicals.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Hydrogenation of Alkenes - Vegetable Ghee Manufacturing
question: In the industrial conversion of liquid vegetable oil into solid vegetable ghee (margarine), hydrogen gas is added across $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bonds in the presence of which heated metal catalyst?

options.A: Finely divided Nickel ($\text{Ni}$) at $200-250^\circ\text{C}$

explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation converts unsaturated liquid fatty acids into saturated solid fats using a Nickel catalyst: $\text{R}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{R}' + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}, \Delta} \text{R}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{R}'$.

subject: Chemistry
question: When an unsaturated alkene (such as Ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$) is bubbled through Baeyer's reagent (cold, dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$), what distinctive visual change confirms unsaturation?

options.A: The purple color of $\text{KMnO}_4$ is completely discharged and a brown precipitate of $\text{MnO}_2$ forms
options.B: The solution turns fluorescent green with no precipitate
options.C: Vigorous evolution of chlorine gas occurs

explanation: Ethene is oxidized to Ethylene Glycol (1,2-ethanediol) by cold alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$, reducing purple $\text{MnO}_4^-$ to brown solid $\text{MnO}_2$, decoloring the purple reagent.

subject: Chemistry
question: When Bromoethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) is heated with alcoholic Potassium Hydroxide (alcoholic $\text{KOH}$), which alkene is prepared via elimination?

options.A: Ethene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$)

explanation: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{KOH}(\text{alc}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{KBr} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Dehydrohalogenation eliminates $\text{HBr}$ to form ethene.

subject: Chemistry
question: Ethyne (Acetylene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) is widely utilized in industrial metal cutting and welding torches because its combustion in pure oxygen (Oxy-acetylene flame) generates temperatures up to:

options.A: $3000^\circ\text{C}$ to $3500^\circ\text{C}$

explanation: The high carbon content and triple bond energy of ethyne produce an intensely hot flame ($3000-3500^\circ\text{C}$) in oxygen, capable of easily melting steel and iron.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Halogen Addition to Alkenes (Bromine Water Test)
question: When liquid Bromine dissolved in $\text{CCl}_4$ (reddish-brown color) is added to Ethene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$), the solution becomes colorless due to the formation of:

options.A: 1,2-Dibromoethane ($\text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$)

explanation: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. Electrophilic halogen addition across the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond discharges the reddish-brown color.

subject: Chemistry
question: Heating Ethanol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) with excess concentrated Sulfuric Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) at $170^\circ\text{C}$ produces:

options.A: Ethene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$) via dehydration elimination of water

explanation: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4, 170^\circ\text{C}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ acts as a strong dehydrating agent.

subject: Chemistry
question: The catalytic reduction of an alkene or alkyne to an alkane using hydrogen gas in the presence of heated Nickel catalyst is named the:

options.A: Sabatier-Senderens Reaction

explanation: The addition of $\text{H}_2$ to unsaturated hydrocarbons over Raney nickel or finely divided Ni catalyst at $200-300^circ\ext{C}$ is named the Sabatier-Senderens reaction.

subject: Chemistry
question: Why do terminal alkynes like Ethyne ($\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{H}$) exhibit weakly acidic behavior, reacting with ammoniacal silver nitrate to form heavy metal acetylide precipitates?

options.A: The terminal carbon is $sp$-hybridized ($50\%\ s$-character), making it more electronegative and able to stabilize the conjugate acetylide anion
options.C: Hydrogen atoms are bonded to oxygen atoms
options.D: Ethyne is an inorganic mineral acid

explanation: High $s$-character ($50\%$) in $sp$-hybridized carbon pulls bonding electron density closer to the carbon nucleus, facilitating release of the terminal proton to strong bases.

subject: Chemistry
question: Natural Gas (Sui gas in Pakistan) utilized domestically and industrially consists predominantly of which alkane hydrocarbon?

options.A: Methane ($\text{CH}_4$, approx. $85-95\%$)

explanation: Natural gas consists predominantly of methane ($85-95\%$) along with minor proportions of ethane, propane, butane, and nitrogen.

subject: Chemistry
question: According to Markovnikov's Rule, when an asymmetrical reagent like Hydrogen Bromide ($\text{HBr}$) adds to an asymmetrical alkene (such as Propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}=\text{CH}_2$), the major product formed is:

options.A: 2-Bromopropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(Br)-CH}_3$)

explanation: Markovnikov's rule states that the electrophilic hydrogen adds to the carbon with more hydrogens, generating the more stable secondary carbocation intermediate to give 2-bromopropane.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Free Radical Halogenation Mechanism of Methane
question: In the photochemical chlorination of Methane ($\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$), what occurs during the 'Chain Initiation' step?

options.A: Homolytic fission of the $\text{Cl}-\text{Cl}$ bond by UV light, producing two reactive neutral chlorine free radicals ($2\text{Cl}^\bullet$)
options.C: Direct fusion of carbon and chlorine nuclei

explanation: Initiation step: $\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{Cl}^\bullet$. UV photon energy matches the chlorine bond dissociation energy ($242\text{ kJ/mol}$), causing symmetrical homolytic cleavage.

subject: Chemistry
question: When Ethene gas ($\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$) is bubbled through cold, alkaline Potassium Permanganate (Baeyer's Reagent), what visual observation and product confirm unsaturation?

options.A: Purple color discharges to form a brown precipitate ($\text{MnO}_2$) while Ethene is oxidized to Ethylene Glycol (Ethane-1,2-diol)
options.C: Solution boils violently into chlorine gas

explanation: Baeyer's test: $3\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + 2\text{KMnO}_4 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 3\text{CH}_2(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2(\text{OH}) + 2\text{MnO}_2\downarrow + 2\text{KOH}$. Purple $\text{KMnO}_4$ decolorizes.

subject: Chemistry
question: Why are terminal alkynes like Ethyne ($\text{HC}\equiv\text{CH}$) weakly acidic, reacting with Ammoniacal Silver Nitrate to form white precipitate ($\text{Ag-C}\equiv\text{C-Ag}$)?

options.A: The terminal carbon is $sp$-hybridized ($50\%\ s$-character), making it strongly electronegative and polarizing the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond to release protons ($\text{H}^+$)
options.B: Ethyne contains sulfuric acid inside its bonds
options.C: Triple bonds are full of hydroxide ions
options.D: Ethyne is an inorganic mineral salt

explanation: Higher $s$-character in $sp$ carbon ($50\%$) holds bonding electrons closer to carbon, stabilizing the acetylide carbanion ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}^-$) and conferring weak acidity ($pK_a \approx 25$).

subject: Chemistry
question: High-density Polyethylene (HDPE) plastic is synthesized by the addition polymerization of Ethene monomer ($n\text{ CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$) in the presence of which transition metal catalyst?

options.A: Ziegler-Natta catalyst ($\text{TiCl}_4 + \text{Al(C}_2\text{H}_5)_3$)

explanation: Ziegler-Natta coordination catalysts enable coordination addition polymerization of ethylene into linear unbranched high-density polyethene (HDPE) under mild conditions.

subject: Chemistry
question: Why is the combustion of Ethyne (Acetylene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) in pure oxygen used extensively in industrial Oxy-Acetylene metal welding torches?

options.A: It burns with an intensely hot flame reaching temperatures over $3000^\circ\text{C}$ to $3300^\circ\text{C}$, sufficient to melt high-grade steel
options.C: It generates zero smoke and zero heat

explanation: The complete combustion $2\text{C}_2\text{H}_2 + 5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ releases immense localized heat, exceeding $3300^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Chemistry
question: When reddish-brown Bromine water ($\text{Br}_2(aq)$) is shaken with an Alkene (such as Cyclohexene or Ethene), what happens immediately?

options.A: The reddish-brown color rapidly decolorizes / disappears as Bromine adds across the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond to form a colorless dibromoalkane
options.D: Bromine water explodes into white sparks

explanation: Electrophilic halogen addition: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ (colorless 1,2-dibromoethane), decolorizing the bromine water.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Catalytic Hydrogenation of Vegetable Oil (Vanaspati Ghee)
question: Liquid polyunsaturated vegetable oils are converted into semi-solid Vanaspati Ghee (margarine) by catalytic hydrogenation in the presence of:

options.A: Hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$) at $150-200^\circ\text{C}$ using finely divided Nickel ($\text{Ni}$) catalyst

explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen across the double bonds of unsaturated fatty acid chains using finely divided nickel at $180^circ\ext{C}$, elevating the melting point to form solid ghee.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Preparation of Alkynes from Vicinal Dihalides
question: Ethyne ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$) is synthesized in the laboratory by the double dehydrohalogenation of 1,2-Dibromoethane using:

options.A: Boiling Alcoholic Potassium Hydroxide ($\text{alc. KOH}$)

explanation: $\text{Br-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-Br} + 2\text{KOH}(\text{alc.}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{HC}\equiv\text{CH} + 2\text{KBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Alcoholic KOH eliminates $2\text{ HBr}$ molecules.

subject: Chemistry
question: Thermal or Catalytic Cracking of high boiling point heavy petroleum fractions ($>\text{C}_{16}$) breaks long alkane chains into:

options.A: Shorter-chain high-octane gasoline alkanes ($C_5-C_{10}$) and valuable alkenes (ethene, propene) for the chemical industry

explanation: Cracking (pyrolysis) uses heat ($500^circ\ext{C}$) and silica-alumina catalysts to break large alkane molecules into higher-demand petrol fractions and monomeric alkenes.
